subject.title: Add testing framework for cron jobs and skills (dry-run mode)

question: Should OpenClaw core own one shared dry-run/testing contract for cron, skills, and tool interception, or should the remaining work stay split across narrower cron-only, global tool dry-run, and skills-runner items?
rationale: The request crosses public CLI/Gateway protocol, cron execution, skill semantics, plugin hooks, and security-sensitive side-effect policy, so code inspection can prove the gap but cannot choose the product boundary safely.

options.title: Design the shared core contract
options.body: Keep this issue as the umbrella and define additive CLI/RPC/config semantics before implementation, with narrower related items feeding into it.

options.title: Split into narrower canonical items
options.body: Use the open global dry-run and scheduled-action issues for those scopes and open or keep a separate skills test-runner issue for the unique skills work.

options.title: Defer the feature
options.body: Leave current force-run and scoped dry-run paths unchanged until test infrastructure becomes a higher roadmap priority.

recommendation.title: Design the shared core contract
recommendation.body: Keep this issue as the umbrella and define additive CLI/RPC/config semantics before implementation, with narrower related items feeding into it.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete authored the prior keep-open review and current blame/history points to Peter Steinberger on the central surfaces.
